Title: Attachment Is the Real Risk
Subtitle: Once something is yours — honest feedback on it starts to feel personal.
LearningGoal: Recognize when emotional attachment to a direction is affecting your ability to evaluate it honestly.

Title: Iteration
Subtitle: Recognize whether a second version was shaped by what the first revealed.
LearningGoal: Recognize whether a second version was genuinely shaped by what the first revealed — or just refined from preference.

Title: Sketching / Quick Visualization
Subtitle: When an idea only exists in your words — pushing back on it means pushing back on you.
LearningGoal: Recognize when a quick sketch would move a conversation faster than words — and know how to make one.

Title: Defining Success
Subtitle: You shipped on time — the demo went well — and nobody can agree on whether it worked.
LearningGoal: Write a checkable success statement before work begins so you can evaluate what you built against what you meant to build.

Title: What Usability Testing Is
Subtitle: Learning what works vs. collecting what people think should work — not the same thing.
LearningGoal: Tell the difference between observing usability and collecting opinions — so you know what kind of evidence you're getting.

Title: Prototype Fidelity
Subtitle: When the prototype looks finished — people stop questioning whether the direction is right.
LearningGoal: Recognize when prototype fidelity is sending the wrong signal — and choose the right level of finish for the question you're asking.

Title: AI as Execution Partner
Subtitle: The output looked complete — everyone moved on — and nobody asked if it was right.
LearningGoal: Recognize which part of a task AI can accelerate and which part requires your judgment — so output speed doesn't replace critical evaluation.

Title: Why You Don't Help During Testing
Subtitle: The participant is going in circles and you know exactly what to tell them. You can't.
LearningGoal: Recognize the moment when helping a participant would corrupt your evidence — and hold back.

Title: Task Statement Design
Subtitle: You wrote it to be clear. What you wrote was a hint.
LearningGoal: Write a usability task that puts participants in a real situation without revealing the interface path they're supposed to find.

Title: Observation Effect
Subtitle: Someone behaves differently when they know they're being watched. So do you.
LearningGoal: Recognize when participant behavior in a session is being shaped by being observed — so you read findings accurately.

Title: Think-Aloud Protocol
Subtitle: You ask someone to think aloud and they go quiet at exactly the wrong moment.
LearningGoal: Recognize when a participant is genuinely thinking aloud versus narrating after the fact — so you know what their words are actually telling you.

Title: What a Prototype Is
Subtitle: You've spent a week on it and the first question back is whether this is even the right approach.
LearningGoal: Recognize a prototype by its purpose — answering a specific question cheaply before committing — not by its form or tool.

Title: Prototype vs MVP
Subtitle: Nobody plans to keep the prototype forever. It just happens.
LearningGoal: Tell the difference between a prototype and an MVP — and catch the failure mode of building one when you mean the other.

Title: No UI as Design Goal
Subtitle: The first AI design conversation is about where the panel goes. Nobody's asked whether it needs one.
LearningGoal: Recognize when the absence of a visible interface is a deliberate design decision — not a missing piece.

Title: Moderated Usability Session
Subtitle: Run a session so you learn where people get stuck — without your help.
LearningGoal: Run a moderated usability session so you learn where people actually get stuck — without your help leading them there.

Title: Unmoderated Usability Testing
Subtitle: Find out where people get stuck without watching them in real time.
LearningGoal: Set up and run unmoderated usability testing so you get behavioral data without being in the room.

Title: AI for Design Work
Subtitle: AI generates fast. Knowing whether to use what it generated takes something else entirely.
LearningGoal: Use AI to accelerate specific design tasks while maintaining judgment over what you keep — modify — or discard.

Title: Paper Sketch Prototype
Subtitle: The room tells you how to refine what you showed. It doesn't tell you whether to build it at all.
LearningGoal: Build and test a paper prototype in under thirty minutes — before any digital tools — and get real feedback the same day.

Title: Lo-fi Wireframe Prototype
Subtitle: Visual design guides users through a broken structure. A wireframe tests it before design can cover for it.
LearningGoal: Build a navigable wireframe that tests whether users can reach their goal — without visual design choices obscuring whether the structure works.

Title: AI-Generated Prototype
Subtitle: It generated fast. Nobody stopped to ask whether it was generating the right thing.
LearningGoal: Use AI to build a functional prototype while controlling for the failure mode where generation speed replaces validation of the question.

Title: Wizard of Oz Prototype
Subtitle: Nobody's sure yet whether users will actually trust the AI feature. Now you can find out.
LearningGoal: Simulate an AI feature's behavior manually in a live session — before the algorithm exists — to learn whether users find it useful and trustworthy.

Title: Conversational Prototype
Subtitle: Script and simulate a conversational flow before writing any code.
LearningGoal: Script and test a conversational flow with a real person before writing any code — so dialogue failures surface in a session instead of production.

Title: High Fidelity Prototype
Subtitle: A hi-fi prototype doesn't just look more finished. It changes what feedback you get — and what you miss.
LearningGoal: Build a hi-fi prototype scoped to the questions only visual quality can answer — and separate visual feedback from structural feedback.

Title: Service Prototype
Subtitle: Every step worked. The journey failed anyway.
LearningGoal: Prototype the full end-to-end service journey — not just the screen — so failures across touchpoints surface before the service launches.

Title: Parallel Prototyping
Subtitle: You asked "does this work?" The question you needed was "which approach works better?"
LearningGoal: Test two or more genuinely different directions simultaneously to get comparative data — not optimization data within one direction.

Title: Build to Think
Subtitle: Wireframes show what you intend. Running code shows what's true.
LearningGoal: Write shallow real code to answer a design question that can only be answered by touching the system — and know when that's faster than describing the answer.
